anomalies.observed: On the SkylabModule sheet, the NTR2101P display-power MOSFET Q3 gate is labeled NET0016, keyboard row ROW6 on U10 pin 22 is also labeled NET0016, and SKW92A U11 pin 41 (I2S_DO) is connected to NET0016. On the EPD_Driver sheet, J4 pin 14 also carries NET0016.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires the display-power switch gate to be driven only by a dedicated SKW92A GPIO with its 10 kΩ pull-up, while keyboard row lines and EPD/SPI signals remain separate nets. The spec states Q2's gate is connected to U5.31 (SKW92A GPIO) and R2 pull-up, and that keyboard column/row lines are wired directly to SKW92A GPIO pins.

evidence.quote: SkylabModule.kicad_sch page 1/4: Q3 NTR2101P gate pin has label NET0016; U10 BBQ10KBD pin 22 ROW6 has label NET0016; U11 SKW92A pin 41 I2S_DO has label NET0016.
EPD_Driver.kicad_sch page 3/4: J4 FH34SRJ-24S-0.5SH(99) pin 14 has label NET0016.
netlist shows `Net-(Q2-G)` = `Q2.1` (gate), `R2.1`→`R2.2`→`+3V3` (10 kΩ pull-up, gate defaults high/off), and `U5.31` (SKW92A GPIO...)

anomalies.impact: The display power MOSFET gate is shorted to a keyboard matrix row and to other module/EPD signal lines. Driving or scanning ROW6, or toggling the EPD/I2S signal on that net, will unexpectedly turn the e-paper display power on or off; conversely, the display-power gate will corrupt keyboard row 6 and the EPD data line.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains a connectivity anomaly: NET0016 merges the display-power MOSFET gate with a keyboard row and other module/EPD signals, contrary to the intended separate GPIO-controlled display power switch.
